title: Completion map is surjective for coherent modules on a proper scheme over a complete base
statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete with respect to an ideal I [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let G,F be coherent O_X-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Using the ideal sheaf I O_X defined by [def-nagata-extended-ideal], the completion map u\mapsto u^\wedge from Hom_{O_X}(G,F) to morphisms between their completions [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], represented in Lean by the map in the corresponding declaration, is surjective.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful); its proof uses Lemma 0882 (lemma-completion-internal-hom) and the theorem on formal functions in the form of Lemma 087U (lemma-spell-out-theorem-formal-functions; Theorem 02OC theorem-formal-functions, Section 02O7 section-theorem-formal-functions)

proof.text: Let H be the internal Hom sheaf. The formal-functions comparison identifies Gamma(X,H) with lim_n Gamma(X,H/I^n H), and the completion-internal-Hom comparison identifies that inverse limit with morphisms between the completed modules. Both comparisons are bijections, and their composite is exactly u |-> u^ by compatibility with reduction modulo I^n. Therefore this composite is surjective.
